text:
maria: Heads up — seeing sustained NVMe write-latency spikes in us-west1 GPU pool starting ~10:28. A bunch of GPU attaches are pending and a few evictions. /cc @aj @simon

devops-bot: ALERT: high-nvme-write-iops on ephemeral pool (us-west1). Affected nodes: gnode-123, gnode-124, gnode-129. Trigger: scratch_io_ops p95 > 45k for 5m.
```
log snippet: gnode-123 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
scrubd: skip due to OOM at 10:29:12
```

aj: Saw the same. scrub/cleaner jobs kicked off at 10:25 then got preempted by large batch runs. Janitor concurrency default=4 so backlog oscillates.

simon: Can we temporarily throttle batch jobs IO or lower their blkio weight? We should also consider nudging `io.scheduler` to mq-deadline fairness on noisy nodes. :thinking:

linda: Quick plan: 1) cordon the worst nodes, drain non-critical batches. 2) move janitor window to midnight SLT and increase scrub concurrency to 8 on low-traffic canaries. 3) add a short-term scheduler routing rule to prefer eu-west for new attaches while we stabilize.

kevin: Doing cordon+drain on gnode-123 now: `kubectl cordon gnode-123 && kubectl drain gnode-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`

maria: Thanks @kevin. Also let's add a temporary fallback policy in the provisioner config so new requests go to eu-west if us-west1 free capacity < 20%. I'll open the scheduler change.

aj: Metrics to watch: `nvme_write_lat_ns.p95`, `scratch_io_ops.total`, `gpu_pending_attach.count`. I'll pin a grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/infrac/ssds (will add threshold annotations).

simon: Minor note — cleaner backoff currently uses exponential with max 5m. If it's getting preempted constantly we should increase concurrency instead of aggressive backoff; I'll drop a patch. PR: #4872.

linda: Reviewed #4872. LGTM for canary. We should run it against 3 canary nodes not whole pool.

kevin: Canary started on gnode-canary-7 with scrub_concurrency=8. Early observation: nvme p95 write latency down from ~120ms -> ~30ms after scrub ramp. :thumbsup:

maria: Great. I'll file an incident ticket and tag oncall for a 1hr watch. Keep posting short updates here.

aj: Will keep an eye on graphs and set a temporary alert on `gpu_pending_attach > 5` for us-west1.

simon: After stabilization we should follow up with infra-ops: increase janitor SLA, and add kube QoS guidance for batch jobs to avoid blkio starvation.

maria: Agreed. Thanks team.
